title: JANUS Face Microcontrol Learning Update v2.0 — From Multiplicity Semantics to Durable World-Boundary Control

learning_arc.stage_1: A semantic investigation of one-source/many-visible-instances/one-world-receipt produced a useful architectural abstraction but failed as a uniqueness claim when ordinary controls matched the visual pattern.
learning_arc.stage_2: The preserved failure taught JANUS to separate internal multiplicity from external effect multiplicity and to separate proposal, world commit, and receipt.
learning_arc.stage_3: Capability scopes and authority epochs showed that correct arbitration is insufficient if permission changes between proposal and dispatch.
learning_arc.stage_4: Cancellation exposed the distributed-systems uncertainty window: after pre-effect validation, no receipt is not the same as no effect.
learning_arc.stage_5: Saga compensation showed that rollback language is often false for the external world. A compensation is another world event and must retain the original event in history.
learning_arc.stage_6: Routing optimization exposed a governance risk: learned competence can become practical censorship unless bounded anti-starvation is constitutional rather than advisory.
learning_arc.stage_7: Crash/restart and multiple workers exposed the gap between logically correct in-memory control and durable operational control, leading to hash-journal replay and generation fencing.
learning_arc.stage_8: Provider retries exposed that idempotency is not a universal property. JANUS must consume an explicit provider capability contract and choose retry policy accordingly.

new_learned_invariants.lesson: Unknown external state must remain unknown until receipt or authoritative reconciliation resolves it.
Canceling future authority cannot erase an effect that may already have crossed the world boundary.
When a settled step must be undone operationally, the undo action has its own provenance, permission, dispatch, and receipt.
Recovery should never overwrite the identity of the failed/canceled authorization; causality remains inspectable.
A correct decision that disappears on crash is not a sufficient control primitive.
Ownership requires a monotonic fencing identity; a process that once owned an effect cannot rely on old local memory after another holder takes over.
Retry safety depends on external semantics. JANUS must model those semantics explicitly instead of assuming them.
Urgency may reorder attention but cannot become a permanent mechanism for silencing old dissent or low-score faces.
When a verification run fails because the verifier itself is wrong, correct the verifier and execute a new full run; never relabel the old failure as success.

micromanagement_model_after_v6_1.faces: generate proposals, criticism, uncertainty estimates, counterexamples, and review requests
micromanagement_model_after_v6_1.routing: may adapt from competence, novelty, risk, deadline, and fairness pressure
micromanagement_model_after_v6_1.authority: remains host/world-bound and is never derived from face count or routing score
micromanagement_model_after_v6_1.dispatch_identity: authorization lineage + fencing generation + optional provider idempotency key
micromanagement_model_after_v6_1.fairness_identity: review ticket with bounded bypass and authority_weight=0

penalize_for_routing_only: silent retry under ambiguous world state

architectural_compression: MANY_FACES -> MANY_PROPOSALS -> ONE_PROTECTED_EFFECT_KEY -> ONE_CURRENT_AUTHORIZATION -> ONE_CURRENT_FENCE_GENERATION -> ZERO_OR_ONE_WORLD_EFFECT_ATTEMPT_UNDER_PROVIDER_POLICY -> AUTHORITATIVE_RECEIPT_OR_UNDETERMINED -> APPEND_ONLY_RECOVERY_HISTORY
why_this_strengthens_janus: The system is becoming less dependent on good intentions and semantic agreement between faces. More invariants are now represented as executable boundaries with receipts, replayable state, and explicit failure modes. This reduces the amount of trust placed in any one face, process, memory, or interpretation.
next_learning_question: Can the mature default Genesis executor be routed through the durable authorization/fencing path under shadow mode first, with deterministic crash injection and provider-specific receipt verification, without regressing current behavior?
